attestation.note: The scope is recorded from the cited article location and the stable arXiv carrier; it is used only to delimit the comparison and not as a premise for the new risk inequalities.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim incorrectly calls the structural intervention likelihood an observational conditional density under an adaptive policy.  The replacement narrows the assertion to the correctly typed structural likelihood, proves the joint-law factorization, and retains exactly the valid cancellation, support, separation, and posterior-variance conclusions.

The numerical certificate is unchanged.  The replacement narrows its interpretation at theorem level by stating that it is a constructive upper certificate, not an all-policy or arbitrary-estimator converse, and by delimiting the exact-carryover regular-design comparator.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: Under outcome-adaptive assignment, the observational conditional density of outcomes given the whole assignment path contains selection effects and does not multiply by the assignment kernel to recover the joint law.  The corrected construction uses the structural path likelihood obtained by intervening on the path before integrating prior latents.

The former prose handle did not define a finite prior family or its payoffs.  The corrected formula enumerates a common null, randomized-offset dyadic block priors with independent block-arm signs, arm-specific lag-band transports, a transport-safe constant multiple of the endpoint radius, and the exact normalized occupancy and information diagnostics.

proposed.name: \ell_Q
proposed.def: For a prior \(Q\) on fixed potential-outcome arrays and a deterministic path \(w\), \(\ell_Q(y;w)\) is the density obtained by intervening to set \(W=w\), evaluating outcomes along \(w\), and integrating the prior latents; it is not the observational conditional density given \(W=w\) under an adaptive experiment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This repairs the likelihood type required for adaptive assignment-factor cancellation.

proposed.name: P_{Q,\pi}
proposed.def: The observed trajectory law induced by a fixed-before-assignment prior \(Q\) and sequential policy \(\pi\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The general-horizon structural factorization and divergence bound need a law notation beyond the horizon-eight worked example.

proposed.name: g_\pi
proposed.def: \(g_\pi(w,y)=\prod_{t=1}^T\pi_t(w_t\mid w_{1:t-1},y_{1:t-1})\), the sequential assignment factor evaluated along a trajectory.

proposed_core_edits.reason: A general common factor makes the structural cancellation well typed for every sequential policy.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The general-horizon prior family is now enumerated and its support, exact randomized-offset block posterior payoff, arm-specific endpoint displacement, structural trajectory factorization, and reverse divergence bound are proved.  The remaining obstruction is a common-measure dyadic stopping argument: the block payoff is averaged under \(\overline Q_b^{\mathrm{blk}}\), while band information is averaged under \(Q_0^{T,L}\).  Assignment-kernel cancellation does not itself transfer occupancy expectations between these laws, and the block perturbation need not have uniformly bounded divergence from the null.  Thus neither the proposed \(1/\log(\mathrm eL)\) certificate nor its no-log refinement is currently a theorem.

statement_notes.justification: This finite-horizon diagnostic now uses a correctly typed structural intervention likelihood and proves the adaptive joint-law factorization before cancellation.
statement_notes.gap: It verifies support, separation, posterior uncertainty, and likelihood cancellation at horizon eight; it is not the policy-uniform occupancy certificate.
statement_notes.consumer: The general multiscale construction reuses its transport and common-factor architecture without treating an adaptive observational conditional density as structural.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma turns the former construction handle into checkable support, posterior-variance, separation, likelihood-factorization, and divergence equations.
statement_notes.gap: Its block and band payoffs are evaluated under different induced path laws, so it deliberately does not claim the missing dyadic stopping certificate.
statement_notes.consumer: Any future proof of the sequential multiscale certificate can start from the two exact normalized payoffs and focus only on charging and change of measure.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the sole prospective all-policy converse after the structural likelihood and finite-family construction have been repaired.
statement_notes.gap: A first-separating-node Carleson inequality must be coupled to a valid transfer between the block-prior and common-null path laws; neither the logarithmic nor no-log form is proved.
statement_notes.consumer: Closing the logarithmic form would yield an unconditional two-sided bracket; removing the logarithm would remain a separate refinement.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem gives the exact finite-horizon certificate, radius-aware scale, and elbow regimes for the Markov truncated Horvitz--Thompson construction.
statement_notes.gap: It is a constructive upper certificate for the all-time GATE, not an all-policy or arbitrary-estimator converse; the cited exact-carryover regular-design result has a different scope and boundary estimand.
statement_notes.consumer: Experiment owners can enumerate the certificate before launch and translate its minimizer into an operational switchback window.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem remains the rigorous implication of a hypothetical no-loss sequential certificate and the proved upper bound.
statement_notes.gap: Its lower premise is open, so the matched all-policy frontier is conditional and is not part of the proved headline.
statement_notes.consumer: A future no-loss certificate would instantiate its premise directly; the presently proved logarithmic certificate is not available.
